clue.text: Set out, in fact, to compose an opera

indicators.note: to compose is to put together or arrange, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resolves, in all seriousness, to write an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compose' turns SETOUT and INFACT into a new arrangement; 'to' is a link. 'Compose' looks like the musical verb that belongs with 'opera', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's comic work of 1790 about fiancées tested for fidelity is one of the best-known operas.

clue.text: Sailor found in hold, transmitting urgent message

indicators.note: a sailor found in a hold is placed inside the word for holding on

parts.note: to hold tight is to cling
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman discovered in a ship's hold is sending a distress call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like a ship's cargo space, but it is the verb meaning grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable was a telegram, so sending one was the way to dispatch a pressing communication.

clue.text: Outlaw immoral sort of woman

definitions.meaning: Will ... is one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws
a '... woman' is the old phrase for a sexually immoral woman

explanation.surface: A bandit is called a wicked kind of woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Will, of that name, is one of Robin Hood's merry men; and the phrase 'scarlet woman' brands a woman as promiscuous.

clue.text: Analysts raise fund for travel

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Psychoanalysts collect money to pay for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travel' rearranges RAISEFUND; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Sigmund Freud practise psychoanalysis, so they are analysts of the mind.

clue.text: Explosive expert exchanging farewell letters with titled person

indicators.note: the letters at the farewell end of the name swap places with each other

parts.note: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite

explanation.surface: A bomb specialist swaps goodbye notes with an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farewell letters' means the final letters: the closing E and L of NOBEL swap round. 'Letters' looks like correspondence, but means alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm, such as a duke or earl, holds a title and belongs to the nobility.

clue.text: Wicked relative acquires a name

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: A villainous family member gets hold of a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquires' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean in the moral sense means impure or sinful, as in the Bible's 'unclean spirits'.

clue.text: Boring to hold on to musical interval

indicators.note: the word for boring is made to hold the next word inside it

parts.note: trite means stale and dull
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something dull clings on to a gap between musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like drilling, but it is the adjective meaning dull; 'hold' is the container signal and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Three whole tones make an augmented fourth, the interval once called the devil in music.

clue.text: Sweet bishop to pronounce on fine church

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to utter is to say or pronounce
scot is an old word for a tax or payment, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A bishop is asked to give a ruling on a handsome church, oddly enough a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'on' are links. SCOT is an old levy, surviving in 'scot-free', meaning without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee-like confection made from brown sugar and butter.

clue.text: Injured feelings, but no opening for silent anger

indicators.note: having no opening means the first letter is dropped from the word for silent

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
rage is fury or anger

explanation.surface: Someone's hurt pride shows itself only as speechless fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no opening' drops the D from DUMB to leave UMB; 'but' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking umbrage means feeling offended or resentful at a slight.

clue.text: Withdrawing support

definitions.meaning: help or endorsement, as for a candidate

explanation.surface: A backer pulls their financial help.
explanation.definitionFit: To back off is to retreat, and backing given to a project is financial or moral help.

clue.text: Practitioner of flight agrees googly is deceptive

indicators.note: a deceptive delivery disguises itself, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bowler concedes that the googly, a cricket ball spinning the unexpected way, tricks the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deceptive' rearranges AGREES and GOOGLY; 'is' is a link. 'Flight' sounds like a bowler's craft in cricket, where a googly is a spin delivery; here it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild grey goose of Europe flies in migrating skeins, so it is a bird that practises flying.

clue.text: Heard place inside was made much bigger

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place goes inside the word for heard

parts.note: a case heard in court has been tried
PL is an abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A court case heard at some venue grew to a great size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' is the legal sense: a judge hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripling a quantity multiplies it by three, which makes it considerably larger.

clue.text: See about backward girl's bad sight

indicators.note: the word for see goes around the next piece

parts.note: to eye something is to see or look at it

indicators.note: backward means the girl's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone notices a girl with poor eyesight walking backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reverses the girl's name to give ESOR. 'bad sight' looks like poor vision but means an ugly view.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, such as a derelict building.

clue.text: Acknowledgement changed at last in this dictionary

indicators.note: the final letter of the radio reply is changed for the last letter of the word at

parts.note: Roger is the radio operator's word acknowledging a message

explanation.surface: An admission was finally amended in this reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' is the last letter of 'at', a T, which replaces the final R of ROGER; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous Thesaurus, a word book of synonyms, a kind of dictionary.

clue.text: What Pavlov's dogs did for literary sister?

definitions.meaning: Pavlov's dogs were conditioned to respond to a bell's ring by salivating
the pen name used by Anne Brontë, sister of Charlotte and Emily

explanation.surface: The question asks how Pavlov's dogs behaved, linking them to a writing sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters wrote as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; Anne was Acton.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it describes the conditioned dogs responding to a ring; as a name it was Anne Brontë's pseudonym.

clue.text: Special team from the business press

parts.note: a task is a piece of business or work
to force is to press or push hard

explanation.surface: A special unit drawn from the financial newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business press' looks like financial newspapers, but splits into two pieces; 'from the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group assembled for one specific mission, as in the military.

clue.text: Gets the hang of navigational aids

definitions.meaning: to compass something is to grasp it in the mind
magnetic instruments that show which way is north

explanation.surface: A new sailor learns to use the instruments for finding the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass as a verb means to understand fully; as nouns, the instruments steer ships and walkers by the needle.

clue.text: Not a brilliant write-up, though it's very powerful

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upwards means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a brilliant is a cut diamond, a gem

explanation.surface: A critic's review is lukewarm though the show is said to be powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write-up' reverses NOTAGEM, read from bottom to top in this down clue; 'though' is a link. 'brilliant' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a cut diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton is an explosive yield equal to a million tons of TNT, hence a hugely powerful bomb.

clue.text: Drug made into solution which one swallows

indicators.note: the word for one takes the next piece inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

indicators.note: a solution dissolves something, so the letters of the word into break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A drug is dissolved in a liquid that someone then drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' scrambles the word into, giving ONIT, and 'swallows' sets that inside the card; 'made' and 'which' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, yields a poisonous plant extract once used medicinally.

clue.text: Scottish maiden with gold and silver

definitions.text: Scottish maiden with gold and silver

parts.note: M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
or is the heraldic word for gold
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Highland lass adorned with gold and silver jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a Scottish girl's name built from a maiden followed by gold and silver. A maiden over is one where no runs are scored in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Morag is a traditional Scottish girl's name, a diminutive of Sarah, so it names a young Scottish woman.

clue.text: Inventor raised sheep with rabbit, we hear

indicators.note: raised means read upwards in this down clue, so the word for sheep turns around

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for rabbit is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: coney is an old word for a rabbit

explanation.surface: An inventor bred sheep alongside rabbits, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RAM into MAR. 'we hear' gives CONI, sounding like CONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi developed long-distance radio telegraphy, winning a Nobel Prize in physics.

clue.text: After study, choose to continue with candidate

indicators.note: choose comes after study, so its word follows in the answer

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Having studied, a party decides to keep the same candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' is the university sense of 'read', as in reading history.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt again is to take up a candidate or policy a second time and keep backing it.

clue.text: Yank stole end of parapet from tower

parts.note: to yank is to tug
a boa is a long feathery or fur stole

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word parapet

explanation.surface: An American pinched the top section of a castle's battlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American and 'stole' like theft; 'tower' is one who tows, not a turret. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat pulls ships into harbour, so it is something that tows.

clue.text: Negotiate terms for entertainment

definitions.meaning: a special pleasure or outing laid on for someone

explanation.surface: Diplomats agree conditions for the evening's party.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating with an enemy means discussing a settlement; a treat is a delight provided for guests.

clue.text: Distant dance-music: old medley

parts.note: far means distant
ragtime, or rag, is syncopated piano dance music

explanation.surface: Far-off dance tunes make an old-fashioned musical mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' looks musical in this surface but means a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or hotchpotch of things.

clue.text: Biblical tribesman's success announced fast

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads as a noun

parts.note: a hit is a success

indicators.note: announced means the word for fast is spoken aloud

parts.note: fast, as in held fast, means tight

explanation.surface: An ancient tribesman's triumph was quickly proclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' makes TITE, which sounds like TIGHT; 'fast' means firmly fixed, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hittites were an ancient people of Anatolia mentioned in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Boisterous suitor changed with love

indicators.note: the letters of suitor are changed in order along with the extra letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A rowdy wooer has been transformed by being in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges SUITOR together with O; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A riotous party is wild and unrestrained, like a riot.

clue.text: A number of theatrical performances

parts.note: a number is one who numbs, working in an operating theatre where the performances are operations

explanation.surface: Several shows put on at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a count but is one who makes numb; 'theatrical' is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctor administers drugs that make patients unconscious during surgery.
